patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH v3] mm/memcontrol: skip non-hierarchical memcg-wide stats when v1 is unavailable

version_history.subject: [PATCH v3] mm/memcontrol: skip non-hierarchical memcg-wide stats when v1 is unavailable

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch optimizes the Linux kernel's memory control group (memcg) statistics by skipping non-hierarchical memcg-wide stats when the v1 version is unavailable. This is done by compiling out the non-hierarchical arrays if CONFIG_MEMCG_V1 is not set, and skipping updates on these arrays even if v1 is supported but blocked by a boot parameter. The patch aims to reduce flush costs by avoiding unnecessary read-modify-write operations, resulting in a 4.1% reduction in memcg-wide aggregation time and a 2.2% reduction in overall flush function time.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 1/2] iommu/arm-smmu-v3: Add a cmdq_entries module parameter
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a new module parameter called cmdq_entries to the iommu/arm-smmu-v3 driver. This parameter allows users to set an upper bound on the number of command queue entries, which is useful for systems with limited memory or those that don't need the maximum hardware-supported queue depth. The requested value is rounded down to a power of two and capped at one page worth of entries, ensuring efficient use of memory while still allowing for command batching to work as expected.

review_comments.author: Nicolin Chen
review_comments.summary: Reviewer Nicolin Chen suggested renaming the 'cmdq_entries' module parameter to 'max_cmdq_depth' for clarity, eliminating the need for rounding down to a power of two.
review_comments.raw_body:
Well, since we want the cmdq depth, why not name the parameter
"max_cmdq_depth"? Then, no rounding and more straightforward.

Nicolin

review_comments.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
review_comments.summary: Author addressed a concern about the parameter name and units, explaining that 'cmdq_entries' does not imply a ceiling, and that the page floor is necessary to prevent failed probes. They also argue that using 'entries' instead of 'log2 depth' is more intuitive.
review_comments.raw_body:
The max_ prefix is better, thanks. cmdq_entries does not say it is a
ceiling.

On the units, the page floor has to stay whatever we call the parameter.

Ask for 8 entries and max_n_shift comes out as 3, which the
CMDQ_BATCH_ENTRIES check in arm_smmu_device_hw_probe() rejects with
-ENXIO. The floor gives you 256 entries on a 4K kernel instead of a failed
probe.

So log2 removes the rounding but not the flooring, and the number asked for
still is not always the number you get. I would rather keep entries than
make people convert.

The rounding is not silent, either: arm_smmu_init_one_queue() already
prints "allocated %u entries for cmdq", so the effective depth lands in
dmesg whichever unit the parameter takes.

On the name itself, "depth" reads to me as a number of entries rather than
its log2, so max_cmdq_depth=8 meaning 256 seems more surprising than the
rounding it replaces.

-- 
  Kiryl Shutsemau / Kirill A. Shutemov

review_comments.author: Nicolin Chen
review_comments.summary: Reviewer suggested renaming the module parameter from 'cmdq_entries' to 'cmdq_max_entries', and also proposed an alternative name for the function 'arm_smmu_queue_max_n_shift'
review_comments.raw_body:
Well, maybe "cmdq_max_n_shift" is a better one over "depth".

Given CMDQ_BATCH_ENTRIES is used, I think cmdq_max_entries works.

Nicolin

review_comments.author: Nicolin Chen
review_comments.summary:
Reviewer suggested minor cosmetic changes to the patch and expressed agreement with its overall cleanliness

Reviewer Nicolin Chen suggested renaming module parameters for clarity, specifically recommending 'ceiling' instead of 'cmdq_entries', and introducing a new parameter '@new_ceiling' to allow overriding the default ceiling.

Reviewer Nicolin Chen suggested moving the natural alignment cap to the beginning of the arm_smmu_cmdq_max_n_shift() function, where it would be applied before calculating the ceiling value.

Reviewer suggested using FIELD_GET() at two call sites to simplify the code and avoid redundant calculations.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 2/2] iommu/arm-smmu-v3: Default queue depths to one page in a kdump kernel
series_items.patch_summary: This patch series modifies the default queue depths for the ARM SMMUv3 driver to one page in a kdump kernel, reducing memory usage and improving performance.

review_comments.author: Nicolin Chen
review_comments.summary: Suggested breaking down the queue depth calculation into two small helpers for better readability.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch allows the queue depths of an ARM SMMU v3 device to be tuned, and reduces their size in a kdump kernel to conserve memory. The command queue depth is made tunable through a module parameter, while the event and priority queues are shrunk to one page by default in a kdump kernel. This change aims to reduce memory usage in a capture kernel without compromising system functionality.
